title: The Atoll — solo dev, survival colony sim where survivors talk in their own voice via live Claude calls (Anthropic API Key required at this point)
author: skunkitomonkito
selftext:
[First 5 minutes of gameplay](https://reddit.com/link/1upuhw5/video/dvasuuwkzsbh1/player)

[Example of an API call conversation](https://reddit.com/link/1upuhw5/video/yh0qpuwkzsbh1/player)

**The Atoll — solo dev, survival colony sim where 13 named survivors talk in their own voice via live Claude calls (not scripted, not local)**

**BYOK - You will need an anthropic API Key to play :/**  

[https://skunkito76.itch.io/the-atoll](https://skunkito76.itch.io/the-atoll) \- Free Download ion [itch.io](http://itch.io)  
(API key set-up instructions in download section)

Hey All,  Just put out an early alpha and wanted to share the AI side of it here since it seems the place to get friendly feedback.

The game: a 13-person castaway colony sim. You direct foraging, building, medicine, expeditions, while a volcano counts down to an eruption. Every survivor has a relationship score that shifts based on what you ask of them and how you talk to them and at the end..... well that would be a spoiler.  

The AI part: survivors speak in live-generated dialogue, in character, reacting to what's actually happened in that specific playthrough: their injuries, who they've lost, how they feel about you. It's Claude (Sonnet), called with the player's own API key, BYOK model — I don't host or pay for inference, key stays local. A full game playthrough with maximum calls runs well under $0.30 in tokens, averaging \~$0.15 for me in testing.

Design-wise, the AI is scoped tight on purpose: it doesn't decide outcomes. All the mechanical stuff like who's hurt, who's dying of thirst, whether an expedition finds anything  runs on deterministic game logic (I've got a skill stat system, called B.U.S.H -  **B**uild**U**tility**S**urvival**H**ealth, that all content is tagged against).   
  
The model only narrates and role-plays within a locked context I hand it: the character's actual history, relationship state, and a hard "these are the only people who exist, don't invent anyone else" constraint (learned that one the hard way, the hallucinations can get *real* creative without them).

Small thing I'm proud of: the ambient sound design is a library of island sounds you can tune to your own taste, or just let the island "breathe" on its own. Not AI, just something I wanted to get right.  The sounds through a headset can be totally relaxing.   I'd like to build on this if people like it. 

It's a slow thoughtful game,  and would suit people who like to read and interact with the characters. But it also has tension,  water and food can be sparse,  and just when you think you think you are thriving,  well, bad things happen.   

Biggest lessons so far:

* Closed-world constraints matter more than I expected. Without an explicit cast list in the prompt, the model will reach for a sister, a friend back home, someone who was never in the story.
* BYOK vs. local is a real tradeoff, not an accident. I get much better prose range than a small local model would give me, but I'm asking players to bring a key, which is real friction.
* I haven't fully solved what happens when the model isn't there. Fallback coverage across AI moments is inconsistent right now,  some have scripted backups if the call fails, most don't yet. Real gap for anyone doing this without a safety net designed in from day one, and it's on my list.

Two things I'd genuinely like thoughts on:

1. **Is BYOK actually going to block most people?** Claude usage is everywhere now, so I don't know if "bring your own API key" is hard dealbreaker for a casual player. I'm planning a potential bundled token system for a later release either way, but I'm trying to gauge how urgent that is.
2. **Are the graphics off-putting?** They're retro/placeholder-tier right now — art is the main thing I'm developing for the next phase. Curious whether the writing and the AI carry it enough to look past that, or whether it's actively pushing people away before they get to the part that matters.
3. **Are the skill games enough for now?**  I'd like to bring in more threaded missions rather than  one off encounters,   probably a few more versions of the skill games too.  Ideas appreciated.

Happy to talk about prompt structure, the stat-vs-narration split, or the hallucination fixes if anyone's fighting the same demons.   
  
Link again if you want to poke at it: [https://skunkito76.itch.io/the-atoll](https://skunkito76.itch.io/the-atoll)

comments.author: Total_Load5775
comments.body:
BYOK feels like the right alpha choice for this, especially because you scoped the model calls to dialogue instead of letting the model decide game outcomes.

The trust-building details I would make very explicit in the UX:

- expected call count / cost before a run
- local-only key storage
- a hard per-session spend or request cap
- graceful fallback dialogue if the provider errors
- a visible reset/delete-key path

The $0.15-$0.30 full-playthrough estimate is honestly one of the strongest parts of the post. It makes the API requirement feel bounded instead of scary.

replies.author: skunkitomonkito
replies.body:
Really useful list, thank you. Going through it against what's actually there right now:

* **Local-only key storage** yes, this one's solid. Key never leaves the player's machine, never touches my servers (I don't have any in the loop).
* **Visible reset/delete-key path** yes, there's an in-game settings option to clear it.
* **Expected call count / cost before a run**  not yet. Right now the $0.15-$0.30 estimate is something I can tell people, not something the game tells them. That should be a pre-run estimate or at minimum a running total, agreed.
* **Hard per-session spend or request cap** don't have this. Good catch, this is probably the most important one on your list,  a runaway loop or an unexpected retry storm shouldn't be able to spend past a ceiling the player didn't set.
* **Graceful fallback dialogue if the provider errors** — this is honestly patchy right now. Some AI moments have scripted fallback if the call fails, most don't yet.  I'm working on a fully offline mode but I think it loses the soul of the game, really depends on feedback.   

Cheers!

replies.author: Total_Load5775
replies.body:
That is a good patch order. I would put the hard cap before the fuller offline mode: estimate calls before the run, stop retries after N provider errors, and require a player opt-in before crossing the cap.

For fallback dialogue, even a simple authored line is better than silence. The important part is making the UI honest: "provider unavailable, using fallback" instead of making the player wonder whether the pause is network, cost, or game logic.

replies.author: skunkitomonkito
replies.body:
Good advice,  I have a list.  I'm taking a few days break and then I'll be back on V2  

Will you try the game?

replies.author: Total_Load5775
replies.body:
Yes, especially once V2 has the cap/running-total work in place.

The bits I would pay attention to as a tester are pretty specific:

- key entry and delete/reset flow
- pre-run cost estimate
- what happens when the request cap is hit
- whether fallback dialogue feels intentional instead of broken
- whether the game clearly explains provider/API errors

For an AI-key game, that trust path is probably as important as the generated dialogue itself. Ping me when the V2 build is ready and I can sanity-check that flow.
